subject: Priority routing flag needed for Velox demo / exception request
messages:
From: Paul Hargrove <paul.hargrove@veloxdata.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Priority routing flag for demo next week

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We have an executive demo scheduled for 2027-07-18 and need to ensure low tail latency for a small subset of requests (50-100 RPS for 10 minutes) during the live run. Our internal infra team asked whether Redwood can apply a temporary "priority-routing" flag that pins traffic to the low-latency variant (higher-cost capacity) without changing our SDK code.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood enable a runtime-level priority flag tied to our API key for the demo window?
- What are the steps and SLA/exception required?
- Any cost/commitment implications for a one-off 10-minute burst?

I've attached our proposed runbook and a screenshot of the latency spike we saw in the sandbox.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can we get a decision by EOD Friday (2027-07-15)?

Best,
Paul
Senior SRE, VeloxData
attachments: screenshot-priority-flag.png, velox-demo-proposal.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Forwarding Paul H.'s ask — Velox needs a short-duration, API-key-scoped priority routing toggle for a live exec demo on 7/18.

Notes / constraints:
- Customer cannot modify SDK; flag must be server-side or via API-key routing.
- They expect minimal downtime and documented rollback — legal/finance have asked about ad-hoc billing.

Karthik / Logan: can you confirm whether we have an existing config toggle (route by key -> high-priority pool) or would this require a manual exception / rollout? If a manual exception, outline steps, owners, and the time to enable/disable.

Tessa — FYI for customer comms and to surface any sales concessions.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Sr. Manager, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority routing flag for demo next week

Kimberly / team,

Short answer: we have an internal routing policy that supports tag-based cohorting per API key, but it isn't exposed to customers as a self-serve toggle. We can do a scoped exception with the following approach:

Plan (minimal-risk exception):
1) Create a temporary route policy named "velox-priority-20270718" that maps Velox's API key to the high-priority GPU pool.
2) Limit scope to a single region (us-west-2) and rate-cap to 150 RPS to avoid noisier cross-region effects.
3) Enable prefix KV cache bypass for that policy to guarantee freshest model state during demo.
4) Observability: create a Dashboard and an alert for latency > 300ms P99 for the cohort; runbook to roll back immediately.

Estimated time to create + QA: 3-4 hours during business day. Enable/disable is a 5-10 minute config flip.

Risk/cost notes:
- This will use reserved/high-priority capacity; incremental cost roughly estimated at $0.06 per 1k tokens for the burst window (rough calc — need finance confirmation).
- We should record the exception in SUP-1239 and run this as an "approved temporary policy" to avoid audit gaps.

Action owners:
- Karthik: build policy and validate in staging (3 hours).
- Logan: prepare the rollback playbook and alerts (1 hour).
- Kimberly/Tessa: confirm with Velox and sign-off on cost.

I can take the lead on the config if you approve.

-karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Priority routing flag for demo next week

Thanks — confirming we'll request customer approval for the estimated incremental cost and the one-off exception. Velox execs need the assurance today so they can update their invite.

I'll ping Paul and get written confirmation (reply-all) then Kimberly can approve internal changes. Happy to help on customer comms.

-tessa

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Paul Hargrove <paul.hargrove@veloxdata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority routing flag for demo next week

Paul — thanks for the quick ask. We can support a short, API-key-scoped priority routing exception for your demo on 2027-07-18 with the constraints below: 

Summary (what we'll do):
- Create and enable a one-off runtime route policy "velox-priority-20270718" scoped to your API key and us-west-2 region.
- Rate cap at 150 RPS and enable KV cache bypass for the cohort.
- Monitoring: we will create a live dashboard and an automated P99 latency alert with a documented rollback.

Costs & approvals:
- Estimated marginal cost is small for a 10-minute window; finance to confirm exact invoicing. This is an exception and will be logged to SUP-1239.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Paul: reply-all confirming you accept the temporary policy and that Redwood may enable/disable during the demo window (please include any billing contact).
2) Karthik: I authorize you to create the policy and validate in staging. Please complete by 7/15 EOD.
3) Logan: prepare rollback playbook and add dashboard.
4) Tessa: coordinate the sign-off and message to Velox execs.

Paul — please reply with the written OK and billing contact and we'll proceed.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Sr. Manager, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
